title: Japanese Black Pine: Ancient Black Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: The pine of the Japanese coast, trained into shapes weather never would. Tokyo's Yogo Pine, over 600 years old, spreads on 82 wooden props.
intro: Pinus thunbergii is the pine of the Japanese coast, tough enough for salt spray and heavy snow, and gardeners have spent centuries training it into shapes weather alone never would. The Yogo Pine at Zenyoji in Tokyo, said to be over six hundred years old, is eight metres tall and spreads over more than eight hundred square metres on eighty-two wooden props; in 1980 a sumo referee was called in to settle whether it or a rival in Kagawa was Japan's finest pine, and ruled them joint champions. Kanazawa strings ropes from a pole above its Karasaki pine every November so wet snow cannot break the limbs, the rigging that has become the picture of the city in winter. Tokyo's Hamarikyu pine grows in a garden the bay still floods on purpose, and Nara's is the fattest survivor of centuries of planting for looks.
